title: Multi-Agent LLM Systems: From Emergent Collaboration to Structured Collective Intelligence
abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) are usually developed and evaluated as solitary agents: a single, monolithic network trained on static corpora and queried one prompt at a time. This single-agent paradigm has produced impressive capabilities, yet it fundamentally mismatches the structure of many real-world problems in science, engineering, and governance, which are inherently multi-actor, iterative, and argumentative. In this Perspective, we argue that the next scaling frontier for LLMs is not simply “bigger models with more data”, but societies of models and tools designed as structured collective intelligences. We first outline why classical scaling laws, which relate performance primarily to parameter counts, token volume, and compute, are insufficient for tasks that require debate, division of labor, and long-horizon coordination. We then introduce a conceptual framework based on three interaction regimes—competition, collaboration, and coordination—and show how different task families naturally demand different regime designs, incentives, and communication protocols. Building on emerging multi-agent LLM systems in reasoning, code generation, and autonomous science, we sketch a research programmer for “multi-agent pretraining”, in which agents jointly learn not only language and world models, but also norms of discourse, peer review, and self-correction. We further discuss how multi-agent architectures reshape scaling laws, evaluation methodology, and safety: performance becomes a function not only of model size and data, but also of team composition, interaction topology, and institutional memory. Finally, we argue that carefully engineered artificial communities may approximate the epistemic dynamics of real scientific communities more faithfully than any single, static model, opening a path toward more robust, transparent, and controllable AI systems.</jats:p>

title: Multi-scenario digital twin-driven human-robot collaboration multi-task disassembly process planning based on dynamic time petri-net and heterogeneous multi-agent double deep Q-learning network
abstract: To reduce the environmental impacts and resource utilization of End-of-Life (EOL) product recycling, it is imperative to achieve the high efficiency of EOL product recycling and reutilization, including disassembly. However, the disassembly of EOL products is being faced with huge challenges due to the uncertainties of EOL product recycling and dynamic disassembly requirements. Therefore, this paper proposes a digital twin (DT)-assisted multi-agent human-robot collaboration (HRC) disassembly system with multi-scenario data simulations to achieve multi-agent disassembly operations and process optimization. In addition, the dynamic disassembly structure based on dynamic Time Petri Net (TPN) model represents the real-time disassembly information and associated disassembly relationships, which incorporates the digital twin technology to simulate the application environment of HRC disassembly operations. By integrating the multi-agent Dueling-Double deep Q-learning network (MADDQN) algorithm to determine the optimal disassembly sequence and associated task strategy in the DT-assisted HRC disassembly platform. Similarly, it is essential to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm for multi-task disassembly planning based on HRC disassembly operations. By conducting an in-depth analysis of the NEV-P50 battery pack from the Weilai ES8 as a case study, the practical implementation of the MADDQN algorithm is demonstrated to optimize the dynamic disassembly sequence and uncertain task allocation with DT data, which provides an effective and flexible approach to the complex disassembly tasks in multi-scenario HRC disassembly processes.

title: MASK: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Optimizing Adversarial Attacks on Multi-Agent Systems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of adversarial attacks on multi-agent systems, which aims to manipulate their decision-making process. Previous works typically employ a single adversary or a Best-of-N strategy to generate reference arguments, which persuades group agents and thus steers the system towards a false conclusion. However, their performance is still far from satisfactory due to limited knowledge, as well as a lack of iterative evaluation and feedback. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a new perspective by leveraging agent systems to enhance adversarial attacks and then proposes a new approach named Multi-Agent Collaboration for Optimizing Adversarial Attacks (MASK). The core of MASK is to utilize three collaborative LLM agents to generate reference arguments for the adversary. Specifically, we first design multiple argument agents that automatically generate diverse candidate reference arguments through multi-round discussions. Subsequently, these candidate sets are aggregated by a summarization agent from various perspectives into a cohesive argument. We also introduce an evaluation agent to assess the validity of the summarized argument and provide feedback for regeneration. The three types of agents are integrated into a closed-loop collaborative framework to enable effective adversarial attacks on multi-agent systems. Experimental results on a range of benchmark datasets demonstrate that MASK outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

title: Generative and Cognitive Artificial Intelligence for Adaptive Human-Machine Collaboration
venue: International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: This paper will examine how Generative AI and Cognitive AI can be combined to create more adaptable, realtime systems, provide more contextual awareness, and improve human-to-machine communication. The main goal is to develop a model that can not only generate content but also reason, learn, and adapt to user inputs and dynamic environmental changes. The combination of the two AI technologies will make the model enhance productivity, creativity, and problem-solving skills in areas like healthcare, education, and the creative industries. The suggested model is tested by experiments in the real-world setting with emphasis placed on the most important performance criteria, including the time of task completion, the correctness of the recommendations, and the satisfaction of the user. The results show that the model works better in a variety of aspects compared to the current human-AI collaboration systems, including IBM Watson and the GPT-3 offered by OpenAI. The accuracy of the recommendations of the model, in particular, was determined to be 92 %, and the confidence interval is 90-94. The user satisfaction was 4.5/5, and with a 95% confidence interval of [4.3, 4.7]. It was found that the time to complete the tasks was 15 % lower than with the traditional models, and proved the efficiency of the processes supported by real-time adaptation. Such findings underscore how a combination of Generative AI and Cognitive AI can be useful in developing more responsive, context-sensitive, and user-friendly AI systems. Further efforts in the future will aim at making the model more flexible within more dynamic and complex environments, more multi-modal to process, and more transparent and explainable, to make the deployment of AI in the real world ethical.

title: Human-AI collaboration in Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems
venue: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunications
abstract: <jats:p>This paper examines Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems, integrating both human and non-human intelligent agents, as a new subject of management research. It presents original definitions of key concepts: intelligent agents, artificial intelligent agents, and Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems. These definitions are grounded in Distributed Artificial Intelligence and provide a foundation for exploring the collaboration between human and artificial intelligent agents. The study addresses fundamental research questions regarding the nature of intelligent agents and their role within Multi-Agent Systems, proposing Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems as a novel framework that allows for seamless cooperation between human and non-human entities. Through a narrative literature review, this paper highlights the potential implications of Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems for scientific research in management, offering a conceptual basis for future research in this evolving field.</jats:p>

title: Multi-Modal Analysis of Presentation Media Data
venue: International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: With the explosive development of multimedia information systems, the fusion analysis of the multi-modal information is a research trend. Inspired by this, this study proposes a presentation media data processing algorithm based on multi-modal analysis, which mainly includes a multi-modal processing framework for image data and video data. This study combines scene graph generation, tensor fusion, user label hyper-graph and other modeling ideas to build a new multi-modal analysis paradigm to solve the problems in multi-modal analysis. For image multi-modal analysis, this study proposed a two-stage prediction model based on scene graph generation, which performs modal feature analysis through modified tensor fusion. For video multi-modal analysis, this study designed a new collaborative filtering algorithm based on user label hyper-graph, which comprehensively considers video activity and the user behavior weight to optimize recommendation effect. More specifically, targeting the dissemination characteristics of demonstration media data, this study finally analyzed the information transmission mode of human-computer combination and designed a dissemination optimization method based on multi-modal information processing. By using data from three public datasets and generating test cases, the experimental results of this study show that this method performs well in terms of accuracy, robustness and other indicators.

title: Beyond Optimization: A Multi-Agent Systems and Human–Agent Collaboration Perspective on Decentralized Multi-UAV Task Allocation
abstract: <jats:p>Decentralized task allocation among multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is a critical NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem for enabling autonomous swarms to operate without central supervision. Multi-UAV research has advanced distributed algorithms to manage physical constraints, dynamic networks, and battery limitations. However, previous work frequently reduces task allocation to abstract numerical cost minimization, largely overlooking the critical socio-cognitive coordination dynamics both among UAVs and with human partners. Furthermore, previous surveys often blend centralized and decentralized architectures, leaving a gap for a dedicated, decentralized multi-agent systems (MASs) perspective. This review addresses these limitations by framing decentralized multi-UAV task allocation as a cooperative coordination problem rather than a simple optimization task. First, we establish a taxonomy that categorizes the literature into four foundational approaches—market-based, learning-based, distributed optimization, and clustering—comprehensively mapping their characteristics and trade-offs. Second, we bridge the multi-UAV literature with broader MAS research, highlighting how socio-cognitive models can address the current optimization-versus-coordination mismatch. Third, we contrast the dominant supervisory control approach of human–UAV collaboration (HUC) with the reciprocal, peer-level teaming models found in human–agent collaboration (HAC). We advocate for the integration of socio-cognitive factors present in cooperative coordination, such as dynamic trust calibration, shared mental models, hybrid intelligence, and ethics, within the allocation loop. Finally, we present a future research roadmap focusing on richer task structures, socially aware rational agents, mixed-initiative allocation, and multi-dimensional process-level coordination metrics. This review provides a holistic understanding for investigating how decentralized multi-UAV task allocation can evolve from rigid supervisory hierarchies toward resilient, adaptive, and human-aligned cooperative teaming models.</jats:p>

title: Collaboration and Coordination in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: <jats:p>The significance of collaboration and coordination in these systems cannot be overstated. They are fundamental to ensuring that individual agents, each with their unique capabilities and roles, can function together effectively. This paper delves into the theoretical foundations and practical mechanisms of collaboration and coordination within MAS, exploring their evolution, key concepts, and real-world applications.</jats:p>
